Where it began

Dinesh Karthik was born in Chennai on 1 June 1985 and took up cricket at ten. Part of his schooling was in Kuwait before he came home to Chennai. He started out purely as a batter and only took the gloves later, when he was playing for Tamil Nadu's youth sides.

He made his first-class debut for Tamil Nadu in late 2002, and an off-season wicketkeeping camp under the former India keeper Kiran More did a great deal for his technique. In the 2003–04 Ranji Trophy he made his first hundred in the semi-final and another in the final against Mumbai.

The player

His Test debut came in Mumbai in October 2004, against Australia, on a turning pitch where 40 wickets fell in two days. He was praised that week for his keeping. Between 2004 and 2018 he played 26 Tests, making 1,025 runs at 25.00 with one hundred and seven fifties, and behind the stumps he took 50 catches and six stumpings.

His best Test year was 2007. Opening the batting, he made his only Test hundred, 129 against Bangladesh in Dhaka, and then scored a fifty in each Test in England. His 263 runs led India's batting as they won a series there for the first time in 21 years.

What made him special

He was quick of hand and eye, a clean hitter and a calm finisher, which made him a valued man in short-form cricket for almost two decades. He was in the squads that won the first T20 World Cup in 2007 and the Champions Trophy in 2013. In the 2018 Nidahas Trophy final, with India needing 34 from two overs, he hit 29 not out from eight balls and won it with a six off the last ball.

Test cricket was harder to pin down. He often came in to cover for others and never quite settled, though he was an extremely good stand-in to have.

Away from the middle

Back in 2006 he became the first Indian to be named man of the match in a Twenty20 international. In 2022, at 37, he was recalled to India's T20 side after three years away and made his first fifty in the format, 16 years after his debut. He captained Kolkata Knight Riders in the IPL, became the first Indian to play in South Africa's SA20, and moved into commentary, joining Sunil Gavaskar as one of only two Indians on the panel for the first World Test Championship final. In 2015 he married the squash player Dipika Pallikal.

And finally

Few careers have had as many second acts. Each time he seemed to be finished, he turned up again with the gloves on and a big hit in hand.
